newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port sale to reduce costs by 60 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port sale to reduce costs by 60 pct - paper.

text.p: The privatization of the key Brazilian port of Santos this year should reduce port costs by 60 percent, daily newspaper Estado de Sao Paulo said.
The government announced earlier this week that it hopes to complete the privatization of the port's terminals by summer.
The port authority Codesp will then invest 200 million reais ($190 million) over the next five years, according to a Transport Ministry advisor quoted in the newspaper.
Codesp will continue as administrator of the port, but will pull out of all port operations, firing 2,500 workers by the end of the year.
"The new port authority will be a third of the cost of Codesp in terms of revenues and spending," said Luis Baldez, special advisor to the Transport Ministry.
The government projects that the volume of cargo handled at Santos will grow to 50 million tonnes within the next four years from 36 million tonnes at present, according to Estado.
Currently, 40 percent of the port is in private hands, representing a third of all cargo moved, it said.
